$comment: Generated by bin/gen-lwmin.mjs from the reference (CONVENTIONS W3, ticket 0016); read by bin/workspace-minimum.mjs. Per routine: `args` are Fortran argument names (options as Fortran letters; SELECT is the number of leading .TRUE. entries), over the grid of bin/gen-lwkopt.mjs; each row ends with the minimum of each of `workspaces`, then the effective minimum of each, then the length each was given while another was measured. A `check` minimum is the smallest length whose call does not return INFO = `info` (min - 1 is rejected); its effective minimum the smallest length at which no callee rejects what the routine passes it either (null: callees reject even at the bound). A `declared` minimum (and effective minimum) is the extent the reference declares. Only rows whose arguments the reference accepts are recorded. `unmeasured`: workspaces with no minimum, and why. `noInfo`: modules whose reference has no INFO argument, so rejects nothing. `noCheck`: modules whose reference never rejects any workspace length (value: the entry hash). `unhandled`: modules the generator cannot measure, and why (bin/lib/lwmin.mjs UNHANDLED).

unmeasured.WORK: LDWORK is its leading dimension, not a length: the JS takes strides (W1), so there is no length minimum to compare

unmeasured.RWORK: declared extent LRWORK names something other than an integer argument
